newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian lending rates have bottomed out, says UBS.
newsitem.headline: Indian lending rates have bottomed out, says UBS.

text.p: Indian lending rates appear to have bottomed out, an economist at UBS Securities said on Wednesday.
"Lending rates have bottomed out," Aditya Samant, UBS economist, told Reuters. "I don't see PLR (prime lending rates) falling below 14.0 percent (per annum)," he said.
"The problem is at the other end," he said, referring to the spread above PLR charged by Indian banks. Most Indian companies are borrowing funds at 16.0 to 18.0 percent, he said.
